references.text: The Lord asks Moses how long the people will refuse to keep His commands, addressing the same theme of the people's disobedience and contempt.
Moses reminds the people that they have been rebellious against the Lord from the day they left Egypt.
A reference to the people's unbelief at Kadesh-Barnea; they did not trust in the Lord and were disobedient.
The psalm describes how the people did not believe in God and did not trust in His salvation.
Despite the signs, the people continued to sin and did not believe in His wonders.
A warning not to harden your hearts as at Meribah and Massah, where their ancestors tested God despite seeing His works.
The people despised the pleasant land and did not believe in the Lord's word.
Continuation of the same event where the Lord speaks about the ten times the people tested Him and refused to listen to His voice.
The signs that God gave Moses to prove that the Lord had sent him—the very same signs the people now reject.
The book of Hebrews refers to this generation as unable to enter because of unbelief.
Even though Jesus had performed so many signs for them, they did not believe in Him—the same pattern of unbelief despite the signs.
